title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
issuing_authority: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
license_or_reuse_notes: Document marked 'Information security code: Open'. Full PDF is NOT redistributed in this repository; only minimal necessary excerpts are stored, with retrieval instructions in scripts/fetch_sources.py.
limitations: Verified: 68 pages, issue/effective/revision dates and code match the PDF cover and page headers. Document contains no numeric acknowledgment clock, no retry rule and no fallback-channel rule for walk-in results; absence of such text in this document is not evidence that no such obligation exists elsewhere.

title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
issuing_authority: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (within Abu Dhabi); OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR for a Dubai case
license_or_reuse_notes: Publicly published by DoH Abu Dhabi. Full PDF not redistributed; minimal excerpts only.
relevant_sections: PP.11.2; PP.11.2(c); PP.11.2(d); PP.11.3 (intro and item a); PP.11.3(b); PP.11.3(c); PP.11.4 (intro and item a); PP.11.4(b)
limitations: Version 1.0 dates from the HAAD era (PDF metadata 2011) and no successor instrument was retrieved. Treat as a comparator whose currency is unconfirmed, not as current Abu Dhabi law.

title: National Patient Safety Goals — Laboratory Program (effective January 2026)
applicability: Applies to Joint Commission-accredited laboratory programmes (not UAE facilities)
license_or_reuse_notes: Joint Commission public standard text; minimal quotation only.
limitations: Applies to Joint Commission-accredited organisations in the United States. Requires the organisation to define timeliness; it sets no number.

title: 2025 SAFER Guide: Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up
issuing_authority: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC), United States
applicability: Applies to US EHR-enabled organisations; used as a comparator for result-tracking safety functions
license_or_reuse_notes: US federal guidance in the public domain; minimal quotation only.
limitations: Published as the 2025 SAFER Guide while the PDF footer reads August 2024; the version mismatch is recorded rather than resolved. Voluntary self-assessment, not a requirement.

title: HL7 FHIR R5 — Task resource
applicability: Interoperability vocabulary for workflow tasks; comparator for state modelling
license_or_reuse_notes: HL7 FHIR specification, Creative Commons licensed; minimal quotation only.
limitations: HTML source: has no page numbers, so page_start is a sentinel (1) and the section anchor is the locator. Task status describes task workflow, not human acknowledgment of result content.

title: Cross-Enterprise Document Workflow (XDW) content profile
issuing_authority: IHE International (IT Infrastructure Technical Framework, Vol. 1, Ch. 30)
license_or_reuse_notes: IHE profile text, short quotation for commentary. HTML source; 'page' is a sentinel (1).
limitations: Profile targets document-sharing workflows between organisations, which a walk-in laboratory result notification does not have.

title: Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
applicability: Architectural framework used for mapping only; the prototype is not a telecom ML deployment
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT only for implementers of ML pipelines; not for clinical facilities
license_or_reuse_notes: ITU-T recommendation, freely downloadable; minimal quotation only.
limitations: Used descriptively to name the architecture components. No conformance claim is made and no certification is implied.

title: AI Ready – Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework, Report 2.0
applicability: Readiness framework used for mapping only
license_or_reuse_notes: ITU publication, freely downloadable; minimal quotation only.
relevant_sections: 2 / AI Policy dimension; 2 / Innovation Ecosystem dimension; 2 / Data dimension
limitations: A readiness framework with no conformance criteria; used only to structure the self-assessment, never as a requirement.

title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
issuing_authority: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
version_or_issue: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
license_or_reuse_notes: Official legislation. Retrieved through browser rendering (the portal returns 403 to scripted clients); minimal quotation only, full text not redistributed.
relevant_sections: Art. 1 (definitions: health information, circulation); Art. 2 (scope, incl. free zones); Art. 4 (confidentiality, validity/credibility, availability); Art. 12 (storage inside the State); Art. 13 (no storage, processing, generation or transfer outside the State without a Health Authority resolution); Art. 16 (patient confidentiality and its five exceptions); Art. 20 (25-year retention); Art. 24 (fine 500k-700k for Art. 13 breach); Art. 25 (disciplinary sanctions 1k-1M)
limitations: Articles are located by article number, not printed page (the portal serves the text as HTML, so only page 1 exists in the extract). Articles 1 and 20 are quoted from the portal text but only Articles 4, 13, 16 and 24 are used as excerpts in this build; the others are recorded as anchors for the report narrative.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL) - unofficial English translation
issuing_authority: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (text); English translation published by Lexis Middle East on a third-party mirror
version_or_issue: As issued; Executive Regulations not yet issued at retrieval
applicability: General personal data. Used here ONLY for the scope exclusion in Article 2, exclusion (e): health personal data subject to legislation regulating its protection and processing falls outside this Decree-Law, which is why the ICT Health Law (U1) governs. PDPL is NOT presented as the applicable health-data instrument.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (national) but EXCLUDED for health data by its own Article 2, exclusion (e) - scope comparators only, never applied to the outcome
license_or_reuse_notes: Official text is Arabic and no official English full text is published on a government domain. This is an unofficial professional translation; minimal quotation only. Provenance is labelled UNOFFICIAL_TRANSLATION everywhere it appears.
relevant_sections: Art. 1 (definition of Sensitive Personal Data, incl. health data); Art. 2 (applicability and exclusions, incl. exclusion (e) health personal data); Art. 10-12 (DPIA triggers, not relied on)
limitations: Translation, not an official English text; article numbering follows the translation. Because the Decree-Law is excluded for health data, no PDPL obligation is used to authorise or prohibit any action - it is cited only to explain which instrument does apply.

title: Policy for Health Information Assets Management (HISHD/PP-12)
issuing_authority: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
applicability: DHA-licensed health facilities in Dubai. Supplies the operational retention duty that restates the federal 25-year floor.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (within Dubai); OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR for an Abu Dhabi case
license_or_reuse_notes: Publicly published by DHA. Full PDF not redistributed; minimal quotation only.
relevant_sections: Section 4.6.1 (retention of HIA for at least 25 years from the last procedure/encounter; retention decisions reserved to the Executive leader/Medical Director)
limitations: Printed page numbers cited (p. 18), not PDF page indices. Retention of communication records is inferred from the definition of a health information asset, not stated for messaging systems specifically.

title: Health Data Quality Policy (HISHD/PP-08)
issuing_authority: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
applicability: DHA-licensed entities in Dubai. Supplies the accuracy obligation and the patient-feedback duty that a corrected critical result has to satisfy.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (within Dubai); OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR for an Abu Dhabi case
license_or_reuse_notes: Publicly published by DHA. Full PDF not redistributed; minimal quotation only.
relevant_sections: Section 4.5.1 (accuracy at aggregate and record level); Section 4.9.10 (entities must implement methods to receive patient feedback regarding inaccurate information); Section 4.9.11 (sanctions for staff violating data-quality policy)
limitations: Printed page numbers cited (pp. 10, 20). Does not itself prescribe a correction workflow; the append-only revision design is a implementation choice, not a quoted requirement.

title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_authority: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
legal_or_guidance_status: OFFICIAL_GUIDANCE (public policy; non-binding, no penalty of its own)
license_or_reuse_notes: Official public policy. Retrieved by rendering the portal page (scripted clients get 403); minimal quotation only, full text not redistributed.
relevant_sections: Introduction; Policy Objectives 1-7; Priorities & Key Components 2 (Safety), 4 (Data Privacy), 5 (Transparency), 6 (Human Oversight), 7 (Governance and Accountability), 12 (Commitment to Treaties and Applicable Laws)
limitations: Rendered text carries no printed page numbers, so excerpts are located by principle number only (page 1 sentinel). Classified OFFICIAL_GUIDANCE throughout: nothing here can become binding at the gate.

title: Abu Dhabi Healthcare Information and Cyber Security Standard (ADHICS V2)
issuing_authority: Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (DoH Information & Cyber Security Office)
applicability: Any entity in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi that generates, accesses, stores, uses, processes or transmits health information. Comparator for a Dubai case; binding for an Abu Dhabi case.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (within Abu Dhabi); OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR for a Dubai case
license_or_reuse_notes: Published by DoH for free download. Minimal quotation only; full text not redistributed. doh.gov.ae fails at TLS for scripted clients from some networks; retrieved by rendering.
relevant_sections: 1 (Standard Scope); 2.30 (Data integrity, definitions). 692 controls across 11 domains in total, of which only the two relied on are quoted.
limitations: Only scope and the integrity definition are excerpted - enough to establish that a cyber instrument applies and to ground tamper-evidence, not enough to claim ADHICS conformance. The rendered text has no printed pagination, so sections are cited by number.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare
issuing_authority: Dubai Health Authority (Health Informatics and Smart Health Department)
applicability: All healthcare facilities and professionals licensed by DHA utilising AI in healthcare services. Applies to the ResultRelay adviser and reviewer agents.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (within Dubai, for DHA licensees using AI)
license_or_reuse_notes: Public DHA policy PDF. Full PDF not redistributed; minimal excerpts only.
limitations: The cover gives a revision date of 01/07/2026, which has passed; no successor was found on dha.gov.ae on 2026-11-02, so currency is unconfirmed. The header shows effective 01/10/2021 while the title block says 1/7/2021.

title: NABIDH Policies and Standards, Section 4: Audit Policy
issuing_authority: Dubai Health Authority (NABIDH health information exchange)
applicability: DHA-licensed healthcare facilities connected to the NABIDH platform, for access to and receipt of PHI through NABIDH.
license_or_reuse_notes: Public DHA policy PDF. Full PDF not redistributed; minimal excerpts only.
limitations: Governs audit logs of NABIDH access, not a laboratory's own messaging system. Used to expose the retention question (3 years for audit logs vs 25 years for health data under Federal Law 2/2019 Art. 20), not as a rule ResultRelay must follow.

title: Regulatory Policy: Mobile Spam
issuing_authority: Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA), now Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA)
applicability: Telecommunications licensees and message senders, for text messages with a UAE link; its operative rules address marketing text messages.
legal_or_guidance_status: BINDING_REQUIREMENT (on telecom licensees); context only for a laboratory
license_or_reuse_notes: Official policy text, retrieved from a third-party copy included in an SMS provider's onboarding pack because tdra.gov.ae does not serve it to scripted clients. Minimal excerpts only.
limitations: Quotes are verified against a third-party copy, not a tdra.gov.ae download. A newer marketing-SMS policy (reported October 2025) may supersede parts of it and was not retrieved.

title: Best practice recommendations: The communication of critical and unexpected pathology results
issuing_authority: The Royal College of Pathologists (United Kingdom)
applicability: UK pathology providers and their clinical users (not UAE facilities).
license_or_reuse_notes: Public RCPath document; minimal quotation with attribution.
limitations: Professional guidance, not law. Its scope is communication to clinical teams; it explicitly does not cover patient-direct communication methods.
